title: aowf-world
label: Nightshade

won.source: The fed's own served Day 4 finale recap; undated in the source beyond "Day 4" of the alliance's first event.

end.source: No further title change is recorded in the held record; this is the belt's only attested reign.

how: Reached three scored falls first in a four-way contest against Shame, Savage Warrior, and Chaos (a running fall-count format, not an elimination match — all four competitors stayed in throughout). Savage Warrior was counted out of the ring at one point, awarding Nightshade a fall under the referee's own ruling without eliminating Warrior, who continued competing and scored two falls of his own. Final score: Shame 2, Nightshade 3, Savage Warrior 2, Chaos 2 — the winning fall a rollup on Shame while Warrior was still recovering.

title: aowf-television
label: Tommy Riley

won.source: The fed's own served AOWF_2 Day 1 broadcast; undated in the source beyond the alliance's second event.

end.source: No further title change is recorded in the held record; this is the belt's only attested reign.

how: Won a three-way Ladder Match over Chad Hazzard and Stephen "the Monkey" MacDonald for the AOWF Television Championship, declared vacant this same broadcast along with every other AOWF title. Chad Hazzard's own manager Lana Jones threw the contested belt into the crowd during the match's own finish; Riley reached it first.
note: A Day 2 (AOWF_1) unification match crowned SOME television champion per Day 4's own back-reference ("three undisputed champions in the TV, IC, and Tag worlds" already crowned), but the served Day 2 text cuts off before naming a winner — that reign, if any, is gap-registered and not asserted here. This row records only the confirmed, textually-resolved AOWF_2 title change; a prior pass's claim that Blade won the Day 2 match was found unsupported by the served text and has been retracted (see blade-aowf's own tenure note).
